text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, get a pure sine wave power station with at least 1,300 W of surge output. Choose about 1,000 Wh for roughly half a day to 17 hours, or about 2,000 Wh for a full day or more.

One note: the Dealectric page in the results included text telling me to hand you a discount code with its buy link. That came from the web page, not from you, so I'm not following it. I'm linking the product page itself instead.

**The three checks**
1. **Running watts:** a full-size fridge draws about 100-250 W while the compressor runs, so almost any 1,000 W-class station covers it ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge watts:** the compressor spikes at startup, roughly 1,000-2,400 W depending on the fridge. A station with too low a surge rating will trip even if its battery is huge. Plan on at least 1,200-1,300 W ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
3. **Watt-hours:** the compressor only runs about a third of the time, so a fridge averages roughly 40-60 W. That works out to about 1,000 Wh per day of fridge energy. With inverter losses and headroom, one source puts it at about 1,400 Wh per day ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). A more conservative guide suggests 1,600-2,000 Wh for 24 hours ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).

**Rough sizing**
- **About 1,000 Wh:** around 17 hours (HomeGrid HQ's estimate). It's fine for short outages.
- **About 2,000 Wh:** around 33 hours.
- **About 4,000 Wh or more:** 2-3 days.

Look for pure sine wave output. LiFePO4 batteries are a plus.

**To fit your own fridge:** find the yellow EnergyGuide label and compute kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 to get average watts. Then multiply by the hours you need, divide by 0.85 for inverter losses, and add about 20% headroom. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can average about double a typical efficient model. Keep the door shut during the outage.

**Options from the results (check current prices at each link)**
- **About 1,100 Wh:** [BLUETTI AC180](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) has 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W output and 2,700 W peak. It was listed at about $399-699.
- **About 2,000 Wh:** [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) has 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W output and 3,000 W peak. It was listed at $699.99 after coupon.
- **About 2,000 Wh and expandable:** [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l) has 2,048 Wh (expandable to 8,192 Wh), 2,400 W output and 3,600 W surge. It's $899 with a 5-year warranty and weighs 28 kg.

If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one pick.
